title: What Is a Point of Sale (POS) System? A Practical Guide for Small Shops
description: What a point of sale (POS) system is, what it records, what you need to use one, and what to look for when choosing a POS for a small shop.
author: Bizora Team

faq.question: What does POS stand for?
faq.answer: POS stands for point of sale: the place and moment where a customer pays for a product or service.

faq.question: Do I need internet to use a POS system?
faq.answer: It depends on the system. Some POS systems need a connection, while others, such as an offline-first app, keep working for your core sales work without internet.

faq.question: Do I need a receipt printer?
faq.answer: No. A thermal receipt printer is useful if you want paper receipts, but many businesses also send receipts through messaging apps or save them as PDF files.

faq.question: Can a POS system track credit sales?
faq.answer: A good POS can. It records the credit sale and the customer who owes the money, so you can follow up and record repayments later.

faq.question: Is a POS the same as a cash register?
faq.answer: Not exactly. A cash register records payments at the counter. A POS system can also keep product, stock, customer and report information connected to each sale.

faq.question: What is the difference between a POS and inventory software?
faq.answer: A POS records sales. Inventory software tracks stock. When the two are connected, making a sale can also update the stock quantity.
